title: Lunch Time at School
intro: It is lunch time for Class 2. We use and to join two ideas that go together.

sections.title: Fill in and.

items.q: Tara has rice ___ dal in her tiffin.
Yusuf washed his hands ___ sat down to eat.
I like apples ___ grapes.

sections.title: Match the two parts with and.
Join the two sentences with and.

items.q: Neha ate a sandwich. Neha drank juice.
items.a: Neha ate a sandwich and drank juice.

items.q: Leo has a red bottle. Max has a red bottle.
items.a: Leo and Max have red bottles.

sections.title: Circle True or False.

items.q: "And" is a joining word.
"Puri and chole" uses and to join two foods.
"And" is a naming word.

sections.title: Write two foods you like. Join them with and.
sections.a: Answers will vary, e.g. "I like idli and sambar."

title: A Rainy Day at Home
intro: It is raining in Bengaluru, so Diya stays home. We use but to join two ideas that are different.

sections.title: Fill in but.

items.q: Diya wanted to play outside, ___ it was raining.
The sky is grey, ___ the house is warm.
I have an umbrella, ___ my brother does not.

sections.title: Circle and or but.
Match the start to the best ending.

items.left: I wanted to fly my kite,
items.right: but the rain did not stop.

sections.title: Circle True or False.

items.q: We use but when two ideas are different.
"I am tired but happy" is correct.
"It rained, but the ground got wet" is a good sentence.

sections.title: Finish this: I like the rain, but ...
sections.a: Answers will vary, e.g. "I like the rain, but I cannot go out."

title: Choosing at the Ice Cream Shop
intro: Kabir is choosing an ice cream at a shop in Jumeirah. We use or to show a choice.

sections.title: Fill in or.

items.q: Do you want a cone ___ a cup?
Kabir can pick mango ___ chocolate.
Should we sit inside ___ outside?

sections.title: Circle and, but or or.

items.before: Would you like a small cup

sections.title: Match each question to its ending.
Circle True or False.

items.q: We use or to show a choice.
"Do you want juice or water?" asks you to choose.
"I ate rice or dal for lunch" means I ate both.

sections.title: Write a question with or about ice cream.

items.q: Use the word or.
items.a: Answers will vary, e.g. "Do you want a cone or a cup?"

title: Holi in the Park
intro: Ananya and her friends are playing Holi in the park. Choose and, but or or.

sections.title: Circle True or False.

items.q: "Do you want pink or blue?" uses the right joining word.
"I fell down and I did not cry" uses the best joining word.
"Mum and Dad played Holi with us" is correct.

sections.title: Circle the correct joining word.

items.before: Do you want a water gun

items.after: it was time to go home.

sections.title: Fill in and, but or or.

items.q: Will you wear a white shirt ___ an old shirt?
Grandma did not play, ___ she gave us gujiyas.
We danced ___ sang Holi songs.
Do you want to play with water ___ dry colours?

sections.title: Join the two sentences with but.

items.q: The colours were bright. The colours were hard to wash off.
items.a: The colours were bright, but they were hard to wash off.

sections.title: Write a sentence about a festival. Use and.
sections.a: Answers will vary; check the sentence uses and correctly.

title: The Global Village Visit
intro: Sana's family visits Global Village in Dubai. Use and, but or or to join the sentences.

sections.title: Join the two sentences with the word in brackets.

items.q: We saw the India stall. We saw the Egypt stall. (and)
items.a: We saw the India stall and the Egypt stall.

items.q: Sana wanted a toy. It cost too much. (but)
items.a: Sana wanted a toy, but it cost too much.

items.q: We can ride the wheel. We can watch the show. (or)
items.a: We can ride the wheel or watch the show.

sections.title: Circle the correct joining word.

items.before: Pick one. Do you want churros

sections.title: Fill in and, but or or.

items.q: The lights were pretty ___ bright.
We were tired, ___ we did not want to go home.
Shall we eat now ___ after the show?
Sana ___ her brother rode the boat.

sections.title: Circle True or False.

items.q: "But" joins two ideas that are different.
"Do you want tea and milk?" is the best way to ask someone to choose one.
We can use and to join two names.

title: Getting Ready for School
intro: Every morning Rhea gets ready for school. Use and to join ideas that go together.

sections.title: Join the two sentences with and.

items.q: Rhea brushed her teeth. Rhea combed her hair.
items.a: Rhea brushed her teeth and combed her hair.

items.q: Papa made toast. Mummy made tea.
items.a: Papa made toast and Mummy made tea.

sections.title: Match the two things that go together.
Fill in and or but.

items.q: Rhea was sleepy, ___ she got up on time.
She ate her cereal ___ drank her milk.
The bus came ___ Rhea got on.
Her brother was ready, ___ he could not find his shoe.

sections.title: Circle True or False.

items.q: "Rhea and her brother" uses and to join two people.
We use and to show a choice.
"I put on my shoes and socks" is a good sentence.

sections.title: Write two things you do every morning. Join them with and.
sections.a: Answers will vary, e.g. "I wash my face and eat breakfast."

title: The Weekend Cricket Match
intro: Yash's team plays cricket every Friday. We use but to show something different or surprising.

sections.title: Match the start to the best ending.

items.right: but we lost by two runs.

sections.title: Circle and or but.
Join the two sentences with but.

items.q: The sun was hot. We kept playing.
items.a: The sun was hot, but we kept playing.

items.q: Dad cannot play. He cheers for us.
items.a: Dad cannot play, but he cheers for us.

sections.title: Circle True or False.

items.q: "We won, but we were happy" is a good sentence.
We often put a comma before but.
"The bat is heavy, but I can lift it" uses but correctly.

sections.title: Finish each sentence your own way.

items.q: We won the toss, but ___
I like batting, but ___
items.a: e.g. I do not like fielding.

items.q: The match was fun, but ___

title: Choosing a Bedtime Story
intro: At bedtime, Ella's Mum lets her choose a book. We use or when there is a choice.

sections.title: Circle and or or.

items.before: Do you want the dragon story

sections.title: Make one question with or.

items.q: Do you want milk? Do you want water?
items.a: Do you want milk or water?

items.q: Shall I switch on the lamp? Shall I switch on the big light?
items.a: Shall I switch on the lamp or the big light?

sections.title: Fill in and, but or or.

items.q: Ella wanted two stories, ___ Mum said only one.
Should we read a short book ___ a long book?
Her teddy ___ her blanket are on the bed.
Is the owl in the story kind ___ mean?

sections.title: Circle True or False.

items.q: "Do you want the red book or the blue book?" asks you to pick one.
"Ella or Mum read together" is a good sentence.
Or is a joining word.

sections.title: Write a question for your family. Use or.
sections.a: Answers will vary, e.g. "Shall we have pasta or rice tonight?"

title: Ganesh Chaturthi at Home
intro: Om's family brings home a Ganesha idol for the festival. Use and, but or or.

sections.title: Fill in and, but or or.

items.q: We made modaks ___ laddoos.
Om wanted to light the lamp, ___ he was too small.
Shall we put the flowers on the left ___ on the right?
Aaji ___ Om sang a song.
The drums were loud, ___ the baby did not wake up.

sections.title: Circle the correct joining word.

items.after: he stayed up for the aarti.

sections.title: Join the two sentences with the word in brackets.

items.q: We bought marigolds. We bought lotus flowers. (and)
items.a: We bought marigolds and lotus flowers.

items.q: The idol is small. It is very pretty. (but)
items.a: The idol is small, but it is very pretty.

sections.title: Circle True or False.

items.q: "And" adds one idea to another.
"Will you come today but tomorrow?" is correct.
"But" means the same as "and".

sections.title: Write a sentence about a festival. Use but.
sections.a: Answers will vary, e.g. "I love Diwali, but the crackers are too loud."

title: An Abra Ride on Dubai Creek
intro: Emma and her Baba ride a small wooden abra boat across Dubai Creek. Join the ideas with and, but or or.

sections.title: Join the two sentences with the word in brackets.

items.q: The abra was small. It was fast. (and)
items.a: The abra was small and fast.

items.q: Emma wanted to sit at the front. It was full. (but)
items.a: Emma wanted to sit at the front, but it was full.

items.q: We can go to the spice souk. We can go to the gold souk. (or)
items.a: We can go to the spice souk or the gold souk.

sections.title: Circle the correct joining word.
Match the start to the best ending.

items.right: and one landed on the roof.

items.left: Shall we take the abra back

sections.title: Circle True or False.

items.q: "The abra was old, but it was safe" uses but correctly.
"Do you want to ride or walk?" asks for a choice.
"We were hungry, or we ate shawarma" is correct.

sections.title: Write about a ride you have taken. Use and or but.
sections.a: Answers will vary, e.g. "The bus was slow, but the ride was fun."

title: The Science Lab Experiment
intro: Class 2 tests which things float and which sink. Some joining words are wrong. Find and fix them.

sections.title: Fix the joining word and write the sentence again.

items.q: Do you want to test the sponge but the spoon?
items.a: Do you want to test the sponge or the spoon?

items.q: I wanted to drop the egg in, or Ms Lee said no.
items.a: I wanted to drop the egg in, but Ms Lee said no.

items.q: Pooja dried the table but her hands.
items.a: Pooja dried the table and her hands.

sections.title: Is the joining word correct? Circle True or False.

items.q: The key sank, but the feather floated.
Shall we test a cork or a key?
The ball floated, but the toy boat floated too.
Ali poured the water and stirred it.

sections.title: Circle the correct joining word.

items.before: Ms Lee gave us a tub
The paper boat floated at first,
items.after: then it got wet and sank.

sections.title: Finish each sentence your own way.

items.q: The pencil floated, but ___
Shall we test a leaf or ___?
I dropped a coin in the water and ___
items.a: e.g. it sank to the bottom.

title: Planting Trees on Earth Day
intro: Class 2 plants trees on Earth Day. Because tells why something happens. So tells what happens next.

sections.title: Circle because or so.
Match the start to the best ending.

items.right: so we put a fence around it.

sections.title: Fill in and, but or or.

items.q: Do you want to dig ___ water the plants?
The spade was heavy, ___ Ravi lifted it.
We planted mango ___ lemon trees.

sections.title: Join the two sentences with because.

items.q: I love trees. They give us fruit.
items.a: I love trees because they give us fruit.

items.q: The birds came. The tree had berries.
items.a: The birds came because the tree had berries.

sections.title: Why should we plant trees? Use because.
sections.a: Answers will vary, e.g. "We should plant trees because they give us clean air."

title: Grandma's Birthday Surprise
intro: Tanvi and Rohan planned a surprise for Grandma. Tanvi made a card, and Rohan baked a cake. Grandma was surprised, but she was very happy. She asked, "Shall we eat the cake now or later?"

sections.title: Read the story. Write the joining word.

items.q: Which joining word shows that Grandma gave a choice? ___
Which joining word adds what Rohan did? ___
Which joining word comes between "surprised" and "she was very happy"? ___

sections.title: Join the sentences. Do not repeat words you do not need.

items.q: Tanvi blew up balloons. Tanvi hung them up.
items.a: Tanvi blew up balloons and hung them up.

items.q: Rohan wanted to sing. Rohan forgot the words.
items.a: Rohan wanted to sing, but he forgot the words.

items.q: Grandma can have tea. Grandma can have juice.
items.a: Grandma can have tea or juice.

sections.title: Read the story. Circle True or False.

items.q: Grandma was surprised and happy.
Rohan made the card.
Grandma asked a question with or.

sections.title: Circle the correct joining word.

items.before: Shall we hide behind the door

sections.title: Write about a surprise you planned. Use but.
sections.a: Answers will vary, e.g. "I made a card for Dad, but he found it early."

title: The Desert Safari Trip
intro: Mateo's family goes on a desert safari near Dubai. Choose and, but, or or because.

sections.title: Circle the best joining word.

items.before: The sand was hot in the day,
Do you want to ride a camel

sections.title: Join the two sentences with the word in brackets.

items.q: Mateo wore sunglasses. The sun was bright. (because)
items.a: Mateo wore sunglasses because the sun was bright.

items.q: The camel was tall. Mateo was not scared. (but)
items.a: The camel was tall, but Mateo was not scared.

sections.title: Circle True or False.

items.q: "Because" tells us why.
"We can sit inside or outside the tent" gives a choice.
"I was cold because I wore a jacket" makes sense.
"And" and "but" mean the same thing.

sections.title: Finish each sentence your own way.

items.q: I like the desert because ___
items.a: e.g. the dunes are fun to slide down.

items.q: We saw a falcon and ___
The dunes were high, but ___
items.a: e.g. I climbed to the top.

title: Packing for a Trip to Shimla
intro: Priya's family is packing for a cold trip to Shimla. Use joining words to make your writing better.

sections.title: Join the sentences with and, but or or.

items.q: Shimla is cold. Priya loves it.
items.a: Shimla is cold, but Priya loves it.

items.q: Shall we take the train? Shall we take the car?
items.a: Shall we take the train or the car?

sections.title: Circle the correct joining word.

items.before: Do you want the blue scarf

items.after: Priya still added one more toy.

sections.title: Match the start to the best ending.

items.left: Priya wanted to bring her bike,

items.right: and put them in the bag.

sections.title: Circle True or False.

items.q: "Priya packed socks or shoes" means she packed both.
A joining word can make two short sentences into one.
"The bag is old but strong" is correct.

sections.title: Write about a trip you would like to take. Use and, but and or.
sections.a: Answers will vary; check and, but and or are each used correctly.
